implementationFindings.finding: The current catch stores String(e.message) (up to 300 characters) and any HTTP transportEvidence. It does not persist e.cause or AggregateError children. Hosted records retain no subcause fields, so “fetch failed” cannot be honestly expanded to a TLS/DNS/timeout diagnosis.

The current classifier uses the outer message and defaults to network; HTTP 503 is consequently broad-classed as network. The retained HTTP/status/body evidence supports the narrower maintenance observation only for Portugal.

The current bounded retry regex inspects the outer message. A nested transient code behind “fetch failed” is not visible to it. Conversely, HTTP 503 can match the bounded retry branch, but actual attempt counts and initial responses were not retained.

Per-source source-evidence JSON is written on successful download. Failure observations are recorded in source-check-results and the queue; an optional raw error body requires SOURCE_REVIEW_RAW_DIRECTORY. Missing failed-source JSON is expected and does not invalidate earlier substantive review.

implementationFindings.scope: public URL validation, fetch timeout and redirects
implementationFindings.finding: The current code validates public HTTPS/DNS, uses manual redirects, a 30-second AbortSignal and bounded hops. A generic fetch failure is not a recorded preflight-DNS error, but fetch may perform its own lookup/connection. Do not declare DNS or TLS successful without the missing transport evidence.

recommendedInstrumentationOnly: Preserve sourceId, attempt index, phase, start/end/elapsed, requested host and validated redirect chain; retain each failed attempt even if a later normal attempt succeeds.

Serialize a bounded allowlist of error.name/message/code/errno/syscall/hostname and nested causes/AggregateError children. Redact credential-bearing URLs/proxy details; never dump process environment, request headers, dispatcher options or arbitrary object graphs.
Record public DNS result/address-family and actual connection diagnostic codes only when safely obtained; keep normal public-address checks and verified TLS enabled.

Classify observed timeout/DNS/TLS/TCP errors from structured evidence. Restrict retries to a bounded policy for demonstrated transient conditions; do not automatically retry certificate errors or access/security responses.
Use fake structured-error tests for ENOTFOUND, UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, ECONNRESET, certificate failures, AggregateError and HTTP 503 maintenance, including preservation of the initial attempt.
Do not resolve editorial issues, change interpretations or refresh substantiveVerifiedAt merely because a later transport succeeds.
